source.title: Deep Learning in Target Space
source.authors: Michael Fairbank; Spyridon Samothrakis; L. Citi

record.tranche_reason: The paper compares a different training parameterization and reports its effect on training-set learning for a classification problem, but does not test the listed versions' conditions.
record.gate_note: The CIFAR and other CNN results report test-set accuracy, not training classification error, so they do not qualify as rows for these versions. The paper's Two-Spirals results explicitly describe training-set learning and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: Section 5.1 and Figure 6 compare learning with and without batch normalization in the same Two-Spirals network using Adam. The authors explicitly report that batch normalization does not help and performs worse. This bears on V6 in a new setting, although the extracted rows omit that comparison.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is substantially correct. The authors conclude that target-space parameterization makes optimization easier and potentially improves generalization, with additional computational cost. They report faster Two-Spirals learning in epochs and stronger long-sequence RNN performance; the claimed smoother optimization surface is supported by their theory and experiments rather than directly quantified here.
record.recipe_differences: Training optimizes activation targets and maps them to weights, rather than directly optimizing weights; the paper compares these approaches.
record.method_sensitivity: The Two-Spirals results vary with optimizer and target-space hyperparameters; the text says reducing the target input batch below the narrowest layer prevents full training-set learning, and increasing λ reduces learning ability. These results do not test a listed version.

fits_no_version.finding: Target-space gradient descent fully learned the Two-Spirals training set in approximately 1,000 epochs; weight-space gradient descent mostly learned it in approximately 40,000 epochs. Target-space iterations cost approximately 3.5 times as much.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For this Two-Spirals network and the separately selected learning rates, target-space training learns the training set in fewer epochs than weight-space training.

record.problems: The CNN test-accuracy table's error margins are standard deviations of just two trials. The relevant Two-Spirals training-set comparison gives no uncertainty estimate.
record.rows_left_out: CNN results in Table 2 report test-set accuracy rather than training classification error, so they were not extracted as rows for the listed versions.

untested.parts: Training classification error on CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100, including corrupted labels and dependence on capacity or training recipe.
Teacher-student ReLU problems, spurious local minima, and additional student neurons.
Training degradation across convolutional-network depths and its prevention by identity shortcuts or special initialization.
Controlled initialization comparisons measuring learning speed or trainable depth; initialization and training parameterization change together here.
Learning rates relative to initial stability thresholds, curvature evolution, recovery, and divergence.
Higher learning-rate tolerance, Fixup, and speed comparisons in the version's named architectures and datasets. Table 2 reports final test accuracy rather than accuracy gain over training.

missing.what: The matched weight-space comparison with and without batch normalization on Two-Spirals. The authors explicitly report no benefit and worse performance with batch normalization. Add comparator rows; numerical curve values are unavailable in the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Its use of Glorot and He initialization does not independently test V4. Final CNN test accuracies do not establish V1 or the speed component of V6.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 training classification error, random or corrupted labels, network size, initialization, optimizer, early stopping, and regularized recipes.
Teacher-student two-layer ReLU problems, spurious minima, and the effect of student width relative to teacher width.
Plain versus residual networks across depth, shortcuts, and normalization, including the cited special-initialization and Fixup conditions.
Comparisons of initialization schemes on learning speed or trainable depth, including orthogonal and Gaussian weights.
Learning-rate behavior around stability thresholds, curvature or sharpness changes, low training loss, and divergence.
Batch-normalization effects on accuracy gain speed and learning-rate tolerance, and comparison with Fixup.

rows.subject: target space
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent in target space on the Two-Spirals classification training set; the reported optimal learning rate was η = 10.
rows.value: fully learn the two-spirals problem’s training set
rows.note: This is a different benchmark from the CIFAR conditions in V1.
rows.check: The reported training outcome is accurate, but target-space performance on Two-Spirals measures no listed version. The network also has all shortcut connections, which the row should specify. Retain as a fits_no_version finding.

rows.subject: weight space
rows.operation_detail: Gradient descent in weight space on the Two-Spirals classification training set; the reported optimal learning rate was η = 0.1.
rows.value: mostly learn the training set only
rows.note: Compared with target-space training; not a CIFAR condition.
rows.check: The reported incomplete training-set learning is accurate, but this weight-space comparator on Two-Spirals measures no listed version. The network has all shortcut connections and Glorot initialization. Retain as a fits_no_version finding.

relationships.condition: Two-Spirals classification with Adam in a tanh 2-5-5-5-2 network with all shortcut connections.
relationships.reason: Based on Section 5.1 and Figure 6, omitted from the rows: batch normalization does not help learning and performs worse than weight-space training without it, qualifying its benefit in this additional setting.
relationships.display_finding: Batch normalization did not improve learning and performed worse than weight-space training without it.
